items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Dizzy says, "Ellman, get off. Get off the band and go get on the bus.

ctx.x: So you all were real aware -- you were very aware of the activities of the Klan and other groups in all the areas that you were traveling through?

Oh, well, I mean, you know that -- you know that they around there, even if the Klan wasn't, the people that were around, they were like -- listen, we play a dance -- we played a dance and -- and -- and a Caucasian gal was looking at -- at Ellman [phonetic sp.], I mean, she's ­ - I mean, she's -- you know, she had a few drinks, man, and -- and she just kept and Dizzy says, "Ellman, get off. Get off the band and go get on the bus. Get out of -- no, don't start any trouble." You know. Because that's just the way it…

When -- when you were touring and playing for dances -- I can remember some of the things I've read about Dizzy's various big bands, sometimes people would expect to hear dance music and sometimes what was being played wasn't really intended to be dance music, but what you all were playing was really intended for dances rather than some of the other tunes that we think of now -­
